claims.statement: For every fixed $`q\in(0,1)`$, constructs compact subsets of $`[0,1]`$ with measure arbitrarily close to one containing no translated and nontrivially dilated copy of $`\{q^n:n\ge1\}`$, with dilations of either sign.
assumptions: q is a fixed real number in (0,1).
Dilations are nonzero real numbers of either sign.
claims.conclusion: For every eta in (0,1), there is a compact set E_{q,eta} contained in [0,1] of measure greater than 1-eta that contains no nontrivial affine copy of {q^n : n >= 1}, for any translation and either sign of nonzero dilation.

leanDeclaration.statement: For every $0<\eta<1$, it constructs a compact set $E\subset[0,1]$ of measure greater than $1-\eta$ that contains no affine copy of $\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}$.

claims.statement: We construct a compact subset of the unit interval, of measure arbitrarily close to one, that contains no affine copy of the dyadic sequence $`\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}`$. The conclusion holds for every translation and every nonzero real dilation, of either sign, proving the dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture.
assumptions: The sequence is the dyadic sequence {2^{-n} : n >= 1}.
Dilations are nonzero real numbers of either sign.
claims.conclusion: There is a compact set E contained in [0,1] with measure arbitrarily close to one that contains no affine copy of {2^{-n} : n >= 1}.

leanDeclaration.statement: For every $0<\eta<1$, it constructs a compact set $E\subset[0,1]$ of measure greater than $1-\eta$ that contains no affine copy of $\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}$.

coverage.scopeExcerpt: The formalization proves the dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture. For every $0<\eta<1$, it constructs a compact set $E\subset[0,1]$ of measure greater than $1-\eta$ that contains no affine copy of $\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}$. Explicitly, for every translation $x$ and every nonzero real dilation $s$, some point $x+s2^{-n}$ lies outside $E$. Both signs of $s$ are included.
